profile.summary: A Rewire study that tests variant scores on simulated rare-disease cases. Each case is one 1000 Genomes person's rare variants in the intellectual disability panel genes (PanelApp 285) plus one inserted ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant; a score succeeds when it ranks that diagnostic first. It compares established lookups (CADD, SpliceAI, REVEL, AlphaMissense), a ClinGen rule-based ranking, and added scores such as AlphaGenome AVI, GPN-MSA, GPN-Star and Evo 2.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: opening, Design

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How often a score, a combined model or a baseline ranks the inserted diagnostic variant first among a case's rare candidate variants (top 1). The primary question is whether adding AlphaGenome AVI to the combined lookups raises top 1 on 500 locked replication cases by at least 5 points.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Findings, Design; PROTOCOL.md section 8

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Backgrounds are 1000 Genomes people's variants in the panel's MANE Select exons plus 20 bp, kept below 1% frequency, then filtered to grpmax below 0.1% using gnomAD v3.1.2 with the person and their family left out, and by the gene's mode of inheritance. ClinVar P/LP background variants are removed. Diagnostics are ClinVar P/LP variants with 2 or more review stars, drawn by class quotas. Three studies: 200 SNV cases and 120 indel cases on the first run's 50 people, and 500 replication cases on 50 new people with no diagnostic position reused. The median list on the 500 is 19 SNVs.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Design; PROTOCOL.md sections 1 to 5

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Models are cross-validated (5-fold, grouped by person) on the 200 and 120, and fitted once on the 200 and applied unchanged to the 500. The primary contrast has a 95% paired interval from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of people, read by a rule fixed in advance with a smallest gain of interest of 5 points; secondary scores use Bonferroni-adjusted intervals. A missing score ranks last. The README reports the primary gain as +1.8 points (-0.4 to +4.0), inside -5 to +5.
sections.source_locator: PROTOCOL.md sections 6, 8 and 11; README.md: Findings and Q1

sections.body: The README lists the scripts in order, run from rare-disease-v2 with uv and Python 3.12. Several inputs come from the first run's data folder and from sibling repositories, and CADD and REVEL scores are refetched because they are not committed.

Realistic filtering: gnomAD frequencies that leave out the person's family, a grpmax filter and an inheritance filter.

ClinVar diagnostics were partly classified with the same lookup tools, which favours the lookups and both baselines; the lookups are near the ceiling at 90.6% top 1.
Run by Rewire with its own code; Evo 2 and the frequency sweep were added after other results were seen and are exploratory, and 944 contrasts are reported.

profile.summary: The read classification part of Hall and Coin 2024: label each non-human read in a sputum-like metagenome as Mycobacterium tuberculosis or not. Kraken2 and minimap2 are each run with three databases, standard and custom, on simulated and artificial real Nanopore and Illumina data. It is for people building culture-free tuberculosis sequencing pipelines who need to choose a classifier and database, including on a laptop.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How accurately each tool and database labels reads as M. tuberculosis, with as few false positives and false negatives as possible, and what it costs in runtime and memory. The authors frame this as a step toward sequencing directly from sputum, where contamination is higher than in culture.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Simulated reads mimic sputum: 46% bacteria, 46% human, 6% M. tuberculosis complex and 1% each virus and NTM, 4.5 gigabases of Nanopore and 0.9 of Illumina. Classification uses the non-human reads left after host removal: 100,733 simulated Nanopore reads, 1,417,015 simulated Illumina pairs, 915,209 real Nanopore reads and 21,172,961 real Illumina pairs. Simulation genomes were kept out of the custom kraken Mycobacterium database.

sections.body: Kraken2 uses the standard, standard-8 and a custom Mycobacterium database; minimap2 uses an M. tuberculosis database, the Clockwork decontamination database and a Mycobacterium genus database. A true positive is an M. tuberculosis read classified as M. tuberculosis. Each configuration is scored by sensitivity, specificity and Youden's index with Wilson score 95% intervals, plus mean runtime and peak memory over 10 runs with 4 threads.

profile.summary: A clinical comparison of two metagenomic workflows for detecting microbes in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid: short-read sequencing on MGI and host-depleted nanopore sequencing (HD-ONT). On 62 BALF specimens, each workflow's organism calls are scored against culture, clinical microbiological tests and a composite reference standard by positive and negative percent agreement. It is for clinical microbiology labs weighing short-read against rapid nanopore metagenomics for pneumonia diagnostics.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether each sequencing workflow finds the organisms that reference methods find in a patient's BALF, and how many extra organisms it reports. The paper also studies mock communities, but the store's protocols cover only the 62 clinical specimens.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Study design

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Residual BALF specimens with traceable culture results were sequenced with the MGI short-read workflow (MGISEQ-200, single-end 50 bp) and the HD-ONT workflow (nuclease and saponin host depletion, GridION R9.4.1). Reads were host-filtered against GRCh38 and classified against a curated database of 20,484 genomes or sequences. A species was called when normalised reads passed RP20M of at least 3 (short read) or RP10K of at least 1 (HD-ONT).
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods, NGS and TGS workflows; Bioinformatic processing; Reference database; Read normalization

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each workflow's organism calls are compared with three references: routine culture; clinical microbiological tests (culture plus qPCR or GeneXpert verification where residual volume allowed); and a composite reference standard that adds organisms detected by both sequencing workflows. Agreement is assessed per organism and summarised as PPA and NPA, restricted to bacteria and fungi. Against the composite standard, the paper reports PPA of 93.3% (NGS) and 90.7% (TGS), and NPA of 77.6% and 83.3%.

limitations.text: Small clinical set (62 specimens) mostly from lower respiratory tract infections; results are specific to these workflows and instruments.

Raw data are in the GSA with no licence stated on the project page read, and there is no code repository or leaderboard.
